title: QBR - VertexCloud health check
next_steps: Send cost breakdown and per-route token analysis
Schedule dedicated capacity sizing / benchmark run
Share SOC 2 Type II package + KMS integration notes
Follow-up meeting to review benchmark results and proposed quote
action_items: Lena Park: Share QBR slide deck + cost breakdown by 2026-08-03
Samir Gupta: Run 1-hour throughput benchmark on a dedicated pool (8k context) - target 2026-08-07
Maya Lin: Provide top 50 prompt set and representative traffic profile - due 2026-08-05
Ravi Patel: Provide network/VPC egress constraints and KMS details - due 2026-08-04
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer exploring move towards dedicated capacity for predictable latency and cost savings; security questions around KMS and SSO checked; next steps include benchmark run and formal quote.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Really appreciate you making time for the QBR. Samir and I are here from Redwood. How's everything on your side?
[00:12] Jules Ortega: Hi Lena, hi Samir, Jules here. All good, busy quarter. Looking forward to the update.
[00:18] Maya Lin: Maya from ML. We've ramped usage a lot, excited to see the cost breakouts.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: Ravi, infra. I have a couple security and network questions.
[00:26] Lena Park: Great — quick agenda: usage and spend trends, reliability incidents and SLA, roadmap fit, security/governance questions, then action items.
[00:35] Samir Gupta: I'll jump into the telemetry and perf numbers in a minute. Quick note: transcript may have some auto-caption errors, apologies if names get munged.
[00:42] Lena Park: Cool. Samir, over to you.
[00:45] Samir Gupta: Yeah, thanks. Ok so looking at the last 90 days — monthly token consumption is up ~3.8x since March, primarily driven by our recommendation flows and some larger batch embedding jobs. Average latency for text-generation p95 across the hosted pool is about 420ms for the 2k context model, embeddings p95 about 180ms. Errors are low — 5xxs have been at ~0.06% but we did see two short incidents in June where a shard had higher tail latency during a GPU driver rollout.
[01:20] Maya Lin: Can you repeat the numbers for embeddings? I think we saw a jump in costs there.
[01:25] Samir Gupta: Sure — embeddings are about 37% of token spend right now because you all are running nightly large-index recomputes. Your monthly embedding units are roughly 1.2B units. Cost per embedding unit on hosted is higher than dedicated inference if you commit. That's one of the levers we wanted to talk about.
[01:42] Jules Ortega: Right, we noticed embedding costs ballooning. The recommendations team runs full re-indexes nightly which is expensive. We're exploring incremental approaches but also want to understand the Dedicated pricing.
[01:52] Lena Park: On dedicated: we typically see a 25-45% reduction in unit cost for heavy steady workloads once reserved capacity is sized correctly, plus you get predictable throughput and lower tail latency because of isolated pools. Samir, want to cover autoscaling and burst?
[02:05] Samir Gupta: Sure — dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. For VertexCloud's current peak TPS pattern, our sizing simulation suggests a 2-node baseline of A100-equivalent with burst to 4 nodes for peaks would cover 99.9% of your demand, with an estimated cost reduction of ~30% in token-equivalent spend after accounting for reserved capacity amortization. But we need to run a short benchmark with your prompt set to validate.
[02:34] Ravi Patel: On network: if we go dedicated or private, our security team requires VPC peering and Egress restrictions; also we must bring our own KMS. Is that supported?
[02:44] Samir Gupta: Yes — Private deployments and Dedicated with Private Control Plane support customer-managed networking. BYOK KMS is supported, we integrate with major KMS providers and HSMs. We do want to validate the exact API calls and key rotations pattern; we have a KMS integration guide.
[02:58] Lena Park: Also — we're SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs, and we can share the compliance pack.
[03:05] Sofia Gomez: One thing from product — we're worried about regressions in quality if we quantize models for cost savings. Is there tooling to monitor regressions?
[03:13] Samir Gupta: Yes — Redwood Optimize tracks quality regressions tied to prompt sets and evals; we can run canary rollouts with a/b tests and auto-fallback if quality drops beyond thresholds. That is, you can route X% to quantized variant and compare metrics.
[03:29] Maya Lin: That sounds promising. Our prompts are very sensitive; even small changes in embeddings hurt recall.
[03:36] Samir Gupta: Totally. For embeddings we usually test 4-bit quantization variants offline and then run a shadow traffic experiment against your top 50 prompts before switching.
[03:45] Jules Ortega: Cool. Back to reliability — those two incidents in June, do you have postmortems?
[03:51] Samir Gupta: We do. Briefly: one incident was a driver mismatch during a rolling kernel update that affected a small fraction of the cluster; rollback and auto-fallback to healthy nodes restored service within 7 minutes. The second was an external network blip in a cloud region which caused a transient increase in latency for requests routed to that region — auto-routing shifted traffic. Uptime across the quarter for our hosted API was 99.95%, meeting SLA, but we flagged the driver rollout process for improved automation.
[04:20] Ravi Patel: Ok that rollback time is acceptable but can you provide more detail on change windows? Our infra team needs maintenance blackout windows.
[04:28] Lena Park: Absolutely — we can provide our maintenance calendar and change window policy. For Dedicated/Private you can control those windows more tightly.
[04:36] Maya Lin: About observability — can we get per-route token-level cost breakdowns and tracing?
[04:41] Samir Gupta: Yes we have per-route dashboards and token-level cost attribution; we can also annotate traces with prompt ids to follow specific flows. We'll share a sample dashboard.
[04:50] Sofia Gomez: On roadmap alignment — what's coming in the next quarter that could help us?
[04:54] Lena Park: A few items: improved quantization profiles with model-specific kernels, better autoscaler heuristics for bursty traffic, and an updated rollout console with easier canary metrics. Also a new feature for cached prefix reuse which should reduce token spend on recommendation flows.
[05:10] Maya Lin: Cached prefix reuse could meaningfully reduce costs for us. Are there any prerequisites?
[05:14] Samir Gupta: We'll need to instrument your prompt prefixes and allow the runtime to maintain KV caches for sessions — it's compatible with current APIs but needs config changes.
[05:22] Jules Ortega: Let's talk about timeframe — if we decide to move to Dedicated, how long to provision and onboard?
[05:29] Samir Gupta: Typical timeline is 3-6 weeks for Dedicated onboarding: sizing and contract, provisioning, migration of traffic with canary, and run benchmarks. Private on-prem can take longer depending on your environment.
[05:40] Lena Park: We can fast-track if you want to start with a pilot reserved pool. We'll send a proposed quote after the benchmark.
[05:47] Maya Lin: On the benchmark — what do you need from us?
[05:50] Samir Gupta: Your top 50 prompts and representative traffic profile, plus a sample index snapshot for embedding tests. If you can provide those, we can reproduce your workload in our staging dedicated pool and run the 1-hour throughput test.
[06:03] Maya Lin: We'll assemble that.
[06:06] Ravi Patel: For security, before we sign any reserved contract, we need the SOC2 package, an architecture diagram, and KMS integration notes.
[06:13] Lena Park: We'll share the SOC2 Type II package and the integration docs. I'll include the architecture diagram and the KMS guide in the follow-up email.
[06:21] Jules Ortega: Great. On pricing — rough numbers for dedicated vs hosted?
[06:26] Lena Park: Ballpark: for your current usage we estimate hosted run-rate of $85k/month. Dedicated with a modest reserved commitment (2-node baseline) would be around $60k/month amortized, plus a small premium for private control plane if you want BYOK. Exact numbers depend on term and burst allowances. We'll provide a formal breakdown.
[06:44] Sofia Gomez: Any penalty for bursting above reserved?
[06:47] Samir Gupta: Burst is metered; there are overage rates, or you can configure dynamic burst credits. We'll show both options in the quote.
[06:55] Maya Lin: Can we run a 2-week pilot first with a short-term reserved discount?
[06:59] Lena Park: Yes — pilot is common. We can do a short pilot with temporary reserved pricing to validate savings.
[07:06] Jules Ortega: OK good. A couple more operational things — audit logs, RBAC, and how long logs are retained?
[07:12] Samir Gupta: Audit logs are retained per plan; standard retention is 90 days, enterprise plans can extend retention and export to your SIEM. RBAC integrates with SAML/SSO, and we support fine-grained roles.
[07:24] Ravi Patel: On SSO — do you support SCIM provisioning?
[07:27] Lena Park: Yes, SCIM provisioning for user sync is supported.
[07:31] Maya Lin: Back to quality: if we do quantization, can Redwood Optimize tie the regressions to specific prompt IDs and alert us?
[07:37] Samir Gupta: Yes — we can set regression thresholds and create alerts tied to prompt sets; if a rollout causes a >X% drop in a prioritized metric (e.g., embed recall), traffic can be automatically shifted back.
[07:49] Jules Ortega: Good. Security and quality both covered. Anything else on usage?
[07:53] Samir Gupta: One more note — there's a pattern where a small subset of long-request sessions (few sessions with very large context windows) account for a disproportionate share of token spend; we can identify and propose adjusted batching or prefix caching to mitigate.
[08:07] Maya Lin: That's likely us — long conversation threads in support assistant. We can look at TTL and session truncation.
[08:12] Lena Park: Excellent. Let's recap next steps: we'll send the QBR deck and cost breakdown, Samir will run the benchmark once we get the prompt set, and we'll share SOC2 and KMS docs. Any objections?
[08:23] Jules Ortega: No objections. Timeline seems reasonable.
[08:26] Sofia Gomez: No objections.
[08:28] Maya Lin: Sounds good.
[08:29] Lena Park: Great — I'll follow up with dates and the benchmark checklist. Thanks everyone.
[08:34] Samir Gupta: Thanks all.
[08:36] Jules Ortega: Thanks. Bye.
[08:38] Conversation end.

Notes about transcription: some technical terms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" as "K-V cash", "quantization" occasionally split). The meeting contained references to shared assets: QBR slide deck (link: <redwood-qbr-deck>), SOC2 package (<redwood-soc2.zip>), KMS integration guide (<redwood-kms-guide.pdf>), and benchmark checklist (<redwood-benchmark-checklist>).
